Peer review happens in other ways in science, too. When researchers apply for grants to fund their 
work, it is often other experts from their field that evaluate their grant proposals and help decide 
whether they should be funded. In a more informal way, researchers are reviewed by their peers 
when they present their findings at a conference. 
Science is often messy and imperfect, but peer-review and publication of results are essential to its 
progress and ability to self-correct when people make mistakes.
